newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Stena Rederi says freezes Finnish ferry order.
newsitem.headline: Stena Rederi says freezes Finnish ferry order.

text.p: Swedish ferry owner Stena Rederi AB said on Friday it would not fulfil a letter of intent with Finnish shipyard Finnyards relating to an order for four high-speed ferries worth around a billion crowns.
"There has been a letter of intent, but we do not intend to fulfil it," a Stena Rederi spokeswoman told Reuters.
Stena Rederi is the main owner of ferry operator Stena Line, but Stena Line spokesman Mats Kling said his company was not affected.
"Right now we're in the middle of introducing the high speed ferries that we have already ordered and further firm orders are not on the agenda," Stena Line spokesman Mats Kling told Reuters.
Kling emphasised that Stena Line and Stena Rederi are two separate companies.
"Stena Line has never signed a letter of intent with Finnyards...Stena Line has not made any undertakings to charter these ferries," he said.
He said Stena Line had its own smaller catamarans in operation and some which were due for delivery soon.
Finnyards confirmed in a statement that Stena Rederi had chosen not to exercise an option to buy four HSS 700 high-speed ferries in 1997/98.
"Yesterday, the shipyard was informed that Stena Rederi had not exercised its option to go ahead with the Stena HSS 700 project for the moment," it said.
Finnyards said that Swedish media reports to the effect that Finnyards had refused to build the ships were incorrect.
Finnyards has already supplied two large HSS 1500 ferries for Stena Rederi, and a third will be delivered in the spring of next year.
